_note: Config for scripts/musique_decompositions_evaluator.py. The composite-score weights and the step-count error scale were hard-coded literals in v1 (0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 and /3.0); they are parameters of the metric, so they live here where a run's config snapshot records them.

break_metrics._note: Knobs of the additive metrics from docs/analysis/2026-08-22-metric-candidates.md (issue #40): the official Break leaderboard trio (EM / SARI / GED, ported from allenai/break-evaluator) and the repaired per-item chain validity. They are ADDITIVE columns and always computed - there is no switch to turn them off, because a metric nobody computes is a metric nobody can check, and none of them enters composite_score, so no published number changes value. Only GED needs parameters, because it is the one expensive metric: the survey measured a single 39-step runaway prediction costing ~115 s of optimizer time on its own. max_nodes_for_optimizer is the ONLY guard that bounds that cost: it is checked before any search starts, and above it the search is skipped and a search-free upper bound (pair nodes in id order, substitute each pair, delete/insert the surplus, keep the edges whose endpoints are both paired, delete/insert the rest) is reported instead - so the value does not depend on how busy the machine was. per_item_time_budget_seconds is only a backstop: the deadline is tested BETWEEN the optimizer's successive approximations, so it cannot interrupt one (including the first), it keeps the last approximation, and the value it produces IS machine-dependent - which is why each firing is counted in ged_fallback_counts, carries its elapsed seconds in the per-item ged_fallback_seconds, and is named in the run note. Break's own evaluator instead DROPS an item that times out, which would break the paired battery (a dropped item has no pair) - see ADR 0026. THE MEASURED COST RECORD lives in ONE place and is generated, not typed: run scripts/ged_cost_benchmark.py (configs/ged_cost_benchmark.json) and it prints the table that docs/adr/0026-break-faithful-metrics-the-implementers-conventions.md carries, with the commit it was measured at. The table is not repeated here, because two prose copies of a measurement drift (PR #44 review, nit 5). What the cap is for, in one line: the optimizer's cost is driven by how closely the predicted step labels tie with the GOLD's labels and by the gold's depth - not by edge count - and 16 nodes is twice the capped decomposer arm's 8-step budget and four times the deepest MuSiQue gold, with the worst case measured at the cap far inside the 20 s budget.

gold_validation._note: The gold rows carry two step-count denominators: the 'hop_count' field (used by the hop-count metrics) and len(question_decomposition) (used by the directional step-count metrics). They must agree or the two families measure different things under one report, so the loader aborts on a disagreement; this caps how many offending ids the error message lists.

paired_comparison._note: Parameters for --compare (paired significance between two per-item files). The bootstrap is resampled from the top-level 'seed' (or --seed), so a comparison is reproducible; iterations, alpha and the mismatch-report cap are parameters of the test, so they live here and land in the run's config snapshot instead of being literals in the script. bootstrap_chunk_size only bounds peak memory (resample indices are drawn this many rows at a time); a fixed seed gives identical results for any chunk size. min_items_for_significance_claim is a REPORTING GUARD, not a statistical standard: below it, every 'significant' flag is additionally marked underpowered, because a handful of items cannot carry a significance claim (McNemar with 3 discordant pairs cannot reach p < 0.05 at all). Jahid and his supervisor own its value.

v1_compat._note: Parameters of the --v1-per-item shim, which lets --compare read v1 prior-work per-item files (the bare-list format with no item_id that predates musique_decomposition_per_item/1) under ADR 0020. default_alignment is how the two files are paired when --v1-alignment is not passed: 'normalized_question' is the alignment docs/analysis/2026-08-20-v1-masking-and-retrieval-significance.md states for its Task A, and it is the default so that note's numbers reproduce from committed code; 'position' pairs the files row by row and exists for v1 artifacts whose question texts are not unique (that note's Task B). read_only_prior_work_root is the v1 repo, which nothing in this pipeline may write into (ADR 0020 condition 1) - the evaluator refuses a --run-dir inside it.
